wealth_origin.summary: His prominence is dynastic and governmental: he belongs to the Al Bu Said dynasty, was named successor by Sultan Qaboos and became Oman's head of state in 2020 after decades of public service. Public sources reviewed do not establish a separate personal fortune or its origin. Oman Investment Authority is the state's sovereign investment arm, so the national assets it manages are not his personal wealth.

confidence.reason: Omani government and succession sources establish his dynastic and public route to prominence, while OIA's own material explicitly describes the authority as the state's investment arm.

biography.plain_text: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said is Oman's head of state and a member of the Al Bu Said dynasty. After completing Oxford's Foreign Service Programme, he worked in the foreign ministry, served as its secretary-general, and spent eighteen years as minister of heritage and culture. Sultan Qaboos named him as successor, and Haitham took the throne in January 2020. His position derives from dynastic succession and decades of public service, not a documented entrepreneurial fortune.

proposed_details.existing_value: Oman's Sultan is Haitham bin Tariq Al Said. Prior to becoming Sultan, he spent decades in the Cabinet of his cousin, Sultan Qaboos bin Said. From 2002 until 2020, he served as The minister of Heritage and Culture. In his will, Sultan Qaboos appointed Haitham as his successor, and he was crowned sultan on January 11, 2020, few hours after Qaboos passed.
